technology.ftsShipsInDays: A tsvector column and a GIN index make search fast enough in days, written by people who already know Postgres.
technology.ftsNothingNew: Nothing new to learn, deploy or page anyone about. The only new concept is a ranking function.
technology.ftsBiggerInstance: A bigger database instance buys some headroom; search queries eat most of it.
technology.ftsRelevanceCeiling: Within two quarters someone asks for typo tolerance, synonyms and facets. Postgres can do some of it, slowly and with effort.
technology.ftsSharedBlastRadius: On Black Friday, searches and checkouts queue for the same database. A slow search becomes a slow payment.
technology.esSetupQuarter: Mappings, an indexing job and a way to keep the index in sync take about a quarter of one engineer's time.
technology.esTokenSpent: A JVM cluster with its own query language, heap tuning and upgrade path: one innovation token, spent on search.
technology.esTwoTruths: Product data now lives in two places. The index lags the database, and someone has to decide which one is right.
technology.esClusterBill: Three nodes running all month, whether anyone searches or not.
technology.esHoldsThePeak: Search is the heaviest read on Black Friday; sent to the cluster, it stops competing with checkout.
technology.esFirstReindex: Within two quarters a mapping change forces a full reindex, and the first one is done at night, by hand, nervously.
technology.shinyLearningCurve: A new language and a graph database cost the team about a quarter of learning before they cost nothing.
technology.shinyTwoTokens: Two innovation tokens at once, for a team of six: a runtime and a data model most of them have never used.
technology.shinyNewRuntime: A second runtime, a second build pipeline, a second way to deploy and observe things.
technology.shinyInfra: A graph database, its backups and a new service's environments, paid monthly from day one.
technology.shinyRecsLift: Recommendations lift orders by a few percent once the graph has enough history. Plausible, unproven.
technology.shinyUnknownFailures: Nobody on the team has seen this graph database fail under load yet. The first time it does, they learn how.
technology.shinyBusFactor: Only one engineer really understands the Elixir service and the graph model. When that person leaves, the team has to learn it in production.
technology.blackFridayBuyers: Black Friday adds about 250 orders a day, and enough of those buyers come back that the bump does not fully fade.
technology.blackFridayFreeze: A week of code freeze and war-room duty before and during the peak. Features wait.
technology.discoveryLicenceAudit: An unusual stack costs more to evidence: the auditor needs it explained before they can sample it.
technology.searchReservoirDry: Catalog reads already go to the search cluster, so the shared Postgres has a little more headroom when it runs dry.

technology.title: Search is slow and Black Friday is coming
technology.concept: Choosing technology: innovation tokens, and why boring technology often wins.
technology.voice: Every new tool is free until somebody has to be paged for it.
technology.briefing: Q4, Year 1. Six engineers, one monolith, one Postgres, and a search box that takes four seconds to say nothing useful. Black Friday is in eight weeks, and someone has already opened a tab about graph databases.
technology.dilemma: Where do you spend your innovation tokens, if anywhere, before the busiest week of the year?
technology.disagreement: Experts disagree here. McKinley's camp says a small company gets a handful of innovation tokens and should spend them only on what makes it different; others answer that the right specialised tool is boring somewhere else, and refusing it just moves the pain into your own code. Both describe real companies.
technology.readNext: Read Choose Boring Technology for the token budget, then the cognitive-load chapters of Team Topologies on what a team can actually carry, then the SRE book on who answers the pager.

postgres-fts.title: Postgres full-text search, on the shared database
postgres-fts.optimizes: Shipping in days with what the team already knows; no tokens spent.
postgres-fts.costs: A relevance ceiling, and search shares a database with checkout.

search-cluster.title: An Elasticsearch cluster for search
search-cluster.optimizes: Good search, and the heaviest read moved off the monolith before the peak.
search-cluster.costs: One innovation token, a second copy of the catalog, and a cluster to run.

discovery-platform.title: A discovery service in Elixir on Neo4j
discovery-platform.optimizes: Recommendations, a modern stack, and a story for the hiring page.
discovery-platform.costs: Two tokens at once, a quarter of learning, and knowledge held by one person.

events.black-friday: Black Friday, 09:00. Traffic triples by noon; a share of the new buyers come back in December.

inspections.postgres-headroom: Site inspection: shared Postgres at about half its capacity and climbing. Whatever got added this year, every order still writes here.
